facts.statement: Charles Lewis Camp described Plotosaurus in 1942 based on fossil specimens found in California, USA.
facts.quote: The taxon was initially described by Berkeley paleontologist Charles Lewis Camp in 1942 from several more or less complete fossil specimens discovered in California, USA.

facts.statement: The earliest specimens of Plotosaurus were found in the Moreno Formation along the San Joaquin Valley, California, in the early 20th century.
facts.quote: The earliest described specimens of Plotosaurus were discovered in the early 20th century from Moreno Formation deposits along the San Joaquin Valley, California.

facts.statement: Allan Bennison discovered a partial Plotosaurus skeleton near Pacheco Pass in 1937.
facts.quote: In 1937 he discovered a partial skeleton from grey sandstone hills near Pacheco Pass during a survey of Late Cretaceous beds in the Diablo Range.

facts.statement: A 2008 study by Lindgren, Caldwell, and Jagt redescribed Plotosaurus using Camp's original specimens and newly uncovered fossils.
facts.quote: A 2008 study by paleontologists Johan Lindgren, Michael Caldwell, and John Jagt redescribed Plotosaurus based on a reexamination of the specimens described by Camp (1942) and new fossils uncovered after it.

facts.statement: Plotosaurus has a morphology converging with ichthyosaurs, indicating more advanced swimming adaptations than other mosasaurids.
facts.quote: Unlike other mosasaurids, Plotosaurus possesses a morphology converging with those of ichthyosaurs, suggesting a much more advanced swimming adaptation than some of its close relatives.

facts.statement: Plotosaurus had fused tail vertebrae, an adaptation for efficient swimming rather than a pathological condition.
facts.quote: Some of the tail vertebrae are fused together; unlike in most mosasaurs this is not a pathological condition but another aquatic adaptation that allowed Plotosaurus to achieve a more efficient swimming design.

facts.statement: Plotosaurus was likely one of the fastest mosasaurs due to its specialized body shape and tail.
facts.quote: These features probably enabled them to also be one of the fastest of the mosasaurs.

facts.statement: The immature holotype of Plotosaurus had a 46 cm skull and was estimated to be 4.2 meters long in total.
facts.quote: The immature holotype of Plotosaurus with 46 cm long skull is estimated to have been 4.2 m long in total, while adults with 1 m long skull would have been larger.

facts.statement: One specimen of Plotosaurus was estimated to reach nearly 8 meters in length and weigh around 1654 kg.
facts.quote: One specimen was estimated to have reached nearly 8 m long and weighed around 1654 kg.

facts.statement: Plotosaurus is classified within the subfamily Mosasaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Mosasaurinae

facts.statement: Plotosaurus has synonyms including Kolposaurus (Camp, 1942) and Garzasaurus (Anderson, 1943, nomen nudum).
facts.quote: synonyms: Kolposaurus Camp, 1942 Garzasaurus Anderson, 1943 (nomen nudum)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Plotosaurus had a wider distribution beyond North America, as fragmentary specimens from Japan may belong to the genus.
facts.quote: Although only known from North America, fragmentary specimens known from Japan that could possibly belong to the genus suggest that it may have had a wider distribution.

facts.statement: A fossil from Chile initially identified as Plotosaurus-like was reidentified in 2019 as possibly belonging to Halisaurus because it did not match Plotosaurus diagnostics.
facts.quote: In 2016, a fragmentary lower jaw discovered in the Quiriquina Formation, near Cocholgüe, Chile, was identified by Eberhard Frey and colleagues as coming from a Plotosaurus-like mosasaur. However, in 2019, Paulina Jiménez-Huidobro and her colleagues discovered that this attribution was erroneous because the fossil did not correspond to the genus diagnostics, the authors reidentifying it as possibly coming instead from a Halisaurus.

facts.statement: Plotosaurus possessed several marine adaptations not seen in other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Plotosaurus poseía varias adaptaciones a la vida marina no vistas en otros mosasáuridos.

facts.statement: Compared to its relatives, it had narrower flippers, a large tail fin, and an aerodynamic fusiform body.
facts.quote: Comparado con sus demás parientes, poseía aletas más estrechas, una gran aleta caudal y un cuerpo fusiforme aerodinámico.

facts.statement: These traits likely allowed it to be a faster swimmer than other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Estos rasgos le permitían probablemente ser nadadores más rápidos que otros mosasáuridos.

facts.statement: It had relatively large eyes suggesting keen vision, and skin impressions indicate it had scaly skin.
facts.quote: También tenían ojos relativamente grandes que sugieren una vista aguda, y las impresiones de su piel indican que tenían una piel escamosa.

facts.statement: Based on cladistic analyses, Plotosaurus is considered the most derived branch of mosasaur evolution.
facts.quote: Basándose en los análisis cladísticos, se considera que Plotosaurus son la rama más derivada de la evolución de los mosasáuridos.

facts.statement: The type species, P. bennisoni, was named by fossil collector Allan Bennison who discovered the first remains in 1937.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, P. bennisoni, fue nombrada por Allan Bennison, un coleccionista de fósiles quien descubrió los primeros restos en 1937.

facts.statement: It measured nearly 9 meters in length and was the first known mosasaur from California.
facts.quote: Medía cerca de 9 metros de longitud, y fue el primer mosasáurido conocido de California

facts.statement: A second species, P. tuckeri, was also found in 1937 by Frank Paiva and Professor William M. Tucker.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, P. tuckeri, fue hallada también en 1937 por Frank Paiva y el profesor William M. Tucker.

facts.statement: Although not as adapted to marine life as P. bennisoni, it was nearly 40% larger, reaching lengths of nearly 13 meters.
facts.quote: Aunque no estaba tan adaptado a la vida marina como P. bennisoni era cerca de un 40% mayor, alcanzando longitudes de cerca de 13 metros.

facts.statement: However, a cladistic analysis by Lindgren, Caldwell, and Jagt (2008) considers P. tuckeri to be a junior synonym.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un análisis cladístico realizado por Lindgren, Caldwell y Jagt (2008) considera a P. tuckeri como un sinónimo más moderno.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Mosasaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mosasaurini

facts.statement: It belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: It is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: It lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
